newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina hopes Brazil won't limit Mercosur imports.
newsitem.headline: Argentina hopes Brazil won't limit Mercosur imports.

text.p: Argentina said Wednesday it hoped the Mercosur customs union was exempted from Brazil's decision to slap restrictions on financing for imports, which has sparked accusations of protectionism.
"We have full confidence and expectations that the measure adopted by Brazil will not include the Mercosur," Argentine Foreign Trade Secretary Jorge Campbell told state-run news agency Telam.
Brazil's Central Bank announced new rules late Tuesday to limit the attractiveness of short-term financing for imports.
Most Brazilian importers with financing of less than 360 days will now have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they retrieve their goods from customs.

Brazil is trying to head off a widening trade deficit, but its regional trading partner Argentina -- which with Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay forms the fledgling Mercosur customs union -- is protestnig the move as "protectionist".

"This has caused concern in the public sector and private sectors of Argentina because it implies restricted access for Argentine exports," said the Undersecretary of Foreign Trade, Alejandro Mayoral.
The Argentine Exporters' Chamber demanded the government "urgently insist that Mercosur exports to Brazil be exempted from this protectionist move."
Campbell said the Argentine envoy to Brazil, Diego Guelar, had been instructed to express "Argentina's great concern about the impact of this move."
He warned that restrictions on Mercosur imports into Brazil would "harm the...credibility of commercial networks that took years to construct."

Argentina and Brazil are already engaged in trade disputes over fiscal subsidies Brazil grants to investments in its poor northeast. Argentine President Carlos Menem is expected to try to unblock the disputes on a visit to Brazil in late April.
